[P1] [PERF-001] PROVEN BOTTLENECK wintage.user.js::onMutations attribute lane

EVIDENCE:
- wintage.user.js:3485-3488 defines MUTATION_RECORD_LIMIT=10000 and ADDED_NODE_BUDGET=500.
- ADDED_NODE_BUDGET bounds only added-node collection/traversal.
- onMutations records are accepted at line 3619 before the 60 ms debounce. noteMutationPressure suspends only when mutationRecords > MUTATION_RECORD_LIMIT, not at the limit.
- Inside the deferred batch, lines 3649-3673 process every attribute MutationRecord synchronously.
- The 500 ms attrCooldown only helps repeated records for the SAME target. Ten thousand distinct targets all take the immediate `process(t, false, w)` branch.
- process() reaches `window.getComputedStyle(el)` at line 3001 before most semantic skipping, so ten thousand unique attribute records can cause ten thousand computed-style reads in one JavaScript task.
- addWorkPressure() is called only after the entire batch at line 3776. Therefore the 600 ms circuit breaker can detect that the task was disastrous only after the task has already monopolized the main thread.
- Audit-only extraction of the real onMutations implementation produced:
  N=500 -> processCalls=500
  N=5000 -> processCalls=5000
  N=10000 -> processCalls=10000
  Each fixture made one post-batch addWorkPressure call and zero continuation requests.
- Existing performance tests strongly cover added-node intake, stylesheet work and force-root work but contain no equivalent per-slice bound for unique attribute records.

ISSUE:
The mutation lane advertises bounded recovery but has an unbounded-within-the-admitted-window attribute path. A legal 10,000-record window can execute 10,000 full process() calls, computed-style reads and queued corrections before yielding once.

The circuit breaker is post-facto for this shape: it can permanently disable JS repainting after the long task, but it cannot prevent the long task that triggered it.

This is especially hostile on framework hydration, virtualized lists, editor surfaces and class/style storms where many unique elements mutate together.

OPTIMIZE:
- Introduce a persistent mutation-batch cursor with an explicit ATTRIBUTE_PROCESS_BUDGET per slice.
- Do not process all unique attribute records inside one 60 ms callback.
- Prefer collapsing attribute records by target before work:
  - retain at most one pending repair per element because process() reads current final DOM/computed state, not historical mutation values;
  - stylesheet-bearing STYLE/LINK state remains separate debt;
  - preserve childList removal bookkeeping separately.
- Drain at most a bounded number of attribute targets per scheduler slice, then yield through the existing floor-limited lane or requestAnimationFrame.
- Check elapsed work periodically during the slice, not only after the complete batch.
- If retained attribute targets exceed a hard cap, promote once to the incremental force lane, which is already a coverage superset.
- Reuse the existing bounded registries rather than introducing another unbounded array/Set.

GUARDRAIL:
- Do not drop the final state of a connected mutated element.
- Preserve self-write identity filtering from flushWrites.
- Preserve STYLE/LINK invalidation and removal-triggered shadow cleanup.
- Preserve attrCooldown semantics for noisy repeated targets.
- The force fallback must remain incremental; overflow must never turn into an immediate document scan.
- Mutation-pressure suspension must remain a last-resort safety mechanism, not become the normal batching primitive.

VERIFY:
- 10,000 UNIQUE class/style attribute records in one delivery: first task performs <= ATTRIBUTE_PROCESS_BUDGET process() and getComputedStyle calls.
- Eventual coverage reaches all connected targets or one explicitly-proven incremental force superset.
- 10,000 records for ONE target collapse to bounded/O(1) retained repair state rather than 10,000 process calls.
- A mixed batch with attributes + STYLE insertion + removals preserves all three debts.
- A deliberately slow process() fixture must yield before MUTATION_WORK_LIMIT_MS is grossly exceeded; breaker decision must occur between slices, not after the whole 10k batch.
- Retained mutation state has an explicit hard bound.
- Existing test-perf-lanes.js, test-repainter-budget.js, test-perf-suspend.js, test-perf-bounded.js and force-root tests remain green.

EVIDENCE:
- GoodEmoji startObserver(), lines 737-763, synchronously loops every MutationRecord and every addedNodes entry directly inside the MutationObserver callback.
- GoodEmoji processNode(), lines 685-711, can perform:
  - querySelectorAll('img');
  - querySelectorAll(reaction selector);
  - a complete TreeWalker traversal of descendant text nodes.
  All occur synchronously before the observer callback returns.
- HideEmbeds observe(), lines 652-665, synchronously loops every added node and executes `n.querySelectorAll(CANDIDATE)`, adding every match to pending Set before schedule() can defer handling.
- RemoveGIFS observe(), lines 331-343, and RemoveStickers observe(), lines 352-366, have the same shape.
- Their requestAnimationFrame scheduler delays handle()/drain(), but NOT candidate discovery or Set retention. The expensive intake has already happened.
- All four plugins can coexist and observe the same Discord update, multiplying synchronous traversal of overlapping newly-added subtrees.
- Audit-only probes against the current plugin classes:
  - GoodEmoji: one 100,000-addedNodes MutationRecord invoked processNode 100,000 times synchronously before return.
  - RemoveGIFS: one added subtree exposing 50,000 candidates caused 50,000 synchronous descendant visits and retained 50,000 Set entries before one RAF.

The plugins batch the SECOND half of work while leaving the FIRST half unbounded.

- Establish one bounded mutation-intake pattern for all four plugins.
- Observer callbacks should perform O(1) or strictly budgeted bookkeeping only:
  - enqueue bounded record/root cursors;
  - schedule exactly one continuation frame.
- Consume MutationRecord.addedNodes incrementally with a persistent index.
- Traverse large added subtrees incrementally instead of calling whole-subtree querySelectorAll/TreeWalker inside the observer callback.
- Ancestor-collapse queued roots so parent+descendant records do not rewalk the same subtree.
- Give pending roots/candidates a hard cap. Overflow should schedule ONE message-list reconciliation/rescan token, not retain one entry per omitted descendant.
- GoodEmoji should use the same bounded traversal lane for images, reactions and text nodes instead of three complete synchronous subtree discoveries.
- Prefer a small shared internal scheduling helper/contract so four plugins do not independently reinvent subtly different unbounded lanes.

GUARDRAIL:
- Do not change GIF/sticker/embed/emoji classification semantics.
- Preserve [data-w95-plugin-ui] exclusion and per-owner row-collapse coexistence.
- Preserve GoodEmoji text/image/reaction coverage and matchSrc behavior.
- Route/list replacement must still be detected.
- stop() must cancel pending frame/intake state and release retained nodes.
- Overflow reconciliation must be a superset and must not repeatedly full-scan while one reconciliation is already pending.

VERIFY:
- One MutationRecord containing 100,000 added nodes: observer callback touches <= small constant/budget and schedules one continuation.
- One added root containing 100,000 candidate descendants: first frame performs <= declared traversal/candidate budget.

- Pending node/candidate retention stays under a declared cap.
- Overflow issues exactly one reconciliation token and eventual behavior matches the current complete scan.
- Run all four plugins simultaneously against the same synthetic insertion and assert the combined per-frame primitive count is bounded.
- stop() during partially-drained intake leaves no pending root/candidate references or scheduled callbacks.
- Existing GoodEmoji, HideEmbeds, RemoveGIFS, RemoveStickers and coexistence functional suites remain behaviorally identical.

[P2] [PERF-003] PROVEN BOTTLENECK wintage.user.js::pruneShadowRegistry shared-observer rebuild

EVIDENCE:
- Every removal-bearing mutation batch can requestShadowPrune() at lines 3775 / 3610-3615.
- pruneShadowRegistry(), lines 3587-3609, synchronously scans EVERY piercedRoots entry to test host connectivity.
- If even one root is dead, it then disconnects the shared shadowObserver and synchronously re-observes EVERY surviving root.
- There is no root budget, continuation cursor or elapsed-work check inside this function.
- The work is not fed into addWorkPressure(), so the generic workload breaker does not account for the prune itself.
- Existing test-perf-lanes.js labels the operation "bounded shadow prune", but its rebuild fixture contains only two roots and therefore does not prove a bound.
- Audit-only execution of the real prune function with one dead final root:
  1,000 registered roots -> 1,000 connectivity checks + 999 observe() calls
  10,000 registered roots -> 10,000 checks + 9,999 observe() calls
  50,000 registered roots -> 50,000 checks + 49,999 observe() calls
  all in one prune invocation.
- The trigger does not establish that the removed subtree contained a shadow host; any removal batch can pay the registry-wide scan.

ISSUE:
The main force/style lanes were carefully made root-budgeted, but shadow cleanup reintroduces an O(R) synchronous side lane, and removal of one root can become roughly 2R root operations because the shared observer has no per-target unobserve.

Large component-heavy pages can therefore produce a latency spike outside the scheduler's advertised root bounds and outside its work-pressure accounting.

OPTIMIZE:
- Make detached-root discovery incremental with a persistent prune cursor and a SHADOW_PRUNE_ROOT_BUDGET.
- Remove the requirement to re-register the entire registry in one task.
- Preferred architecture: stop using one all-or-nothing observer registration set where removing one target requires rebuilding every survivor.
- Viable bounded options:
  1. per-root observers, with incremental registry pruning and disconnect only for dead roots; or
  2. observer shards/chunks capped to a small number of roots, so a dead root rebuilds at most one bounded shard.
- If a shared observer is retained, construct replacement registration incrementally while the old observer remains live, then swap without a blind mutation window; duplicate delivery during overlap must be safely deduplicated.
- Account prune work in diagnostics/work-pressure metrics.

GUARDRAIL:
- No shadow mutation may be lost during observer migration.
- Detached roots must become collectible.
- No repeated full-registry retry loop.
- Removal-only batches must still eventually trigger cleanup.
- Live roots must keep exactly one effective observation path after migration.
- New shadow roots arriving during prune must be assigned to a valid current observer generation.

VERIFY:
- 50,000 registered roots + one dead root: no task may inspect/register more than SHADOW_PRUNE_ROOT_BUDGET + fixed constant.
- Cleanup completes incrementally and the dead root is eventually removed.
- Survivors remain observed throughout the transition.
- Mutations injected during prune/rebuild are delivered exactly once logically.
- Repeated removal batches while a prune is already pending do not create N concurrent scans.
- Suspension/teardown releases every observer shard/root reference.
- Extend test-perf-lanes.js with a large-root primitive-count gate and a RED control restoring the current full-registry prune.
